provider: Open-Meteo (data: Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service, CAMS)
dataset: Air Quality API – current modelled PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, O₃ and air-quality indices for major world cities
description: Current modelled air quality for about 150 major cities worldwide from the CAMS European (11 km) and CAMS global (45 km) atmospheric composition forecasts, as served by the Open-Meteo Air Quality API. Forecast-model values, not station measurements.

coverage.geographic: Global, sampled at a fixed list of 157 large cities and national capitals (cities.json, derived from Natural Earth populated places, public domain). CAMS European 0.1° forecast inside Europe, CAMS global 0.4° forecast elsewhere.

updateCadence.upstream: CAMS global forecast every 12 hours, CAMS European forecast every 24 hours; hourly time steps

attribution: Air quality data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0), based on CAMS European air quality and CAMS global atmospheric composition forecasts – Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) information

license.name: CC BY 4.0 – free API tier for non-commercial use only; CAMS data under the Copernicus licence
license.notes: Open-Meteo terms (https://open-meteo.com/en/terms): the free API may be used for non-commercial purposes only, with fewer than 10,000 API calls per day, 5,000 per hour and 600 per minute; each requested location counts as one call. This adapter makes 2 requests (157 location-calls) every 3 hours, about 1,260 calls per day, on top of the calls of the open-meteo-weather source from the same IP address. The Air Quality API documentation states that all users of Open-Meteo data must provide a clear attribution to the CAMS ENSEMBLE data provider as well as a reference to Open-Meteo. Commercial deployments need a paid Open-Meteo subscription.

limitations: All values are MODELLED: they come from the CAMS atmospheric composition forecast for the grid cell containing the city (about 11 km in Europe, about 45 km elsewhere), not from monitoring stations. Street-level and station readings can differ substantially, and local sources (traffic, fires, dust) are smoothed out or missed.

Outside Europe the 45 km global model is known to over- or under-estimate particulates in desert-dust and biomass-burning regions; extreme values (US AQI above 300) should be checked against local station networks.
Only a fixed sample of 157 cities is polled, every 3 hours, to stay within the free tier's call limit.
The US AQI is defined on 24-hour (PM) and 8-hour (ozone) averages; Open-Meteo computes it from rolling model averages, so it is indicative rather than an official index value.
confidenceNotes: These are MODELLED values from the CAMS forecast, not station measurements, and no per-value uncertainty is published, so records carry no confidence value. Severity is derived by this application from the US AQI bands supplied by Open-Meteo: 0–50 → 0, 51–100 → 1, 101–150 → 2, 151–200 → 3, 201 and above → 4.

retention.note: One record per city, updated in place at every poll; records are purged 2 days after their last model time.

layers.name: Air quality – major cities (modelled)
layers.description: Current modelled PM2.5 and US / European air-quality index for about 150 major cities (CAMS forecast via Open-Meteo). Not station measurements.
